name: High Plank
summary: An isometric bodyweight core exercise held at the top of a push-up position to build anterior core stability and shoulder endurance.

setup: Start on all fours with your hands placed directly underneath your shoulders, fingers spread comfortably.
Step your feet back one at a time to extend your legs, supporting your weight on your hands and the balls of your feet with feet hip-width apart.
Press the floor away through your palms to spread your shoulder blades and create a straight line from your head to your heels.
steps: Lock your position by bracing your abdominals, squeezing your glutes, and engaging your quadriceps.
Hold this rigid straight-arm position for the target duration without allowing your hips to sag or hike upward.
Lower your knees gently to the floor when the set is complete.
instructions.breathing: Breathe continuously and evenly through your nose and mouth without releasing abdominal tension.

common_faults.fault: Sagging at the hips and hyperextending the lower back.
common_faults.correction: Tuck your pelvis slightly under and aggressively brace your core and glutes to restore a neutral spine.

common_faults.fault: Piking the hips up into a tent shape to relieve core tension.
common_faults.correction: Lower your hips until your shoulders, hips, and ankles align in a straight plane.
Actively push through your hands to keep your upper back slightly rounded and shoulder blades protracted.

precautions: Those with wrist discomfort can elevate hands on parallettes or perform the movement on their forearms.
